metric: TE = mean |I_t - W(I_{t-1}, V_t)| over pixels with M_t > 0.5 — KB §11 Core Metrics / Temporal
purpose: Measure the temporal-error baseline for every EXISTING rung before Model D is trained, so M6's margin can be pre-registered against the CNN across-seed spread rather than chosen after seeing the result (KB Decision 46's construction, applied to a new metric).
objective: 1*L1 + 0.5*LPIPS(alex)  — the objective every ladder rung trained under (KB Decision 41). Stated because a TE comparison across rungs is only about architecture if the objective is held fixed.

split.pairing_rule: (f-1, f) with BOTH ends inside the validation split, so the two sequence-start frames contribute no pair: 166 val frames -> 164 pairs, not 166.
split.selection_set_note: This split is also the checkpoint-selection set for every model scored here (KB Decision 35), so these are selection-set figures, not a clean generalisation estimate. TE itself was never a selection criterion — checkpoints were chosen on val_l1 — so it is not directly optimised, but it is measured on frames the selection touched.

mask.shared: One mask per pair, computed from ENGINE buffers only and shared by every source, so two sources cannot be scored on different pixels.

gating: dt_eq_1 is the headline gate (training is 100% dt==1). dt_gt_1 is reported separately as out-of-distribution robustness: those pairs were recorded at a reduced rate during the long reappearance gaps and carry ~8x the displacement. Tick deltas are computed from each record's own 'tick' field.
sharpness_caveat: TE MUST NOT BE READ WITHOUT THE SHARPNESS COLUMN. A blurrier renderer has trivially lower temporal error — blur removes the high-frequency content that sub-pixel misalignment turns into error. This is KB Decision 53's RCS confound on a new metric, and it is not hypothetical here: Model C already sits below M4's 0.90 sharpness floor, so the rung most likely to post a low TE is the one already known to be too soft.
measurability_warning: READ THIS BEFORE USING dt_eq_1 AS A GATE. 43 of the 44 dt==1 validation pairs displace by under HALF A PIXEL (median 0.26 px; only one pair exceeds 1 px), and 63 of the 120 dt>1 pairs are exactly static. The held-out sequences are the two 8-second reappearance rungs, which park the camera for most of their length — KB Decision 35 recorded that property for the qualitative strips and it lands here too. Consequence: on this split TE is very nearly the plain frame difference |I_t - I_{t-1}|, and warp_gain_vs_unwarped is ~0.95 for every source, i.e. warping makes it slightly WORSE because bilinear resampling costs more than a quarter-pixel of alignment buys. TE here still measures temporal STABILITY (flicker), which is a real property and is what separates the models from their teacher — but it does NOT measure reprojection quality, so M6's exit criterion as stated would be won by whichever model flickers least. See by_motion_bucket and motion_response_diagnostic. This is a property of the SPLIT, not of the warp: the warp is verified correct on frames that do move (renderer/temporal/tests/test_warp.py, median 2.04x error reduction).
no_training_note: No model was trained, fine-tuned or re-selected by this run. Every checkpoint is the committed one.

native_engine.gating_note: dt_eq_1 is the HEADLINE gate: training is 100% dt==1, so it is the in-distribution set. dt_gt_1 is an out-of-distribution robustness figure (~8x the displacement) and must not be averaged into it.
native_engine.role: The engine's own render. Deterministic, so this is the temporal-error floor that the warp plus the scene's own disocclusion allows — not zero.

pairs_omitted_too_few_kept_pixels.rule: a pair is dropped when the confidence mask keeps < 5000 pixels; dropped pairs are omitted, never imputed

guard_band_gate.role: THE M6 EXIT GATE (KB Decision 55). The validation rungs park the camera, so TE there measures flicker, not reprojection. These 3 contiguous ranges are dropped from both splits by guard_frames=60, so no model saw them in training or selection, and they carry the 4-second rungs' real motion.

cnn_across_seed_spread.note: The spread M6's margin is pre-registered from. It is a CNN quantity measured over 3 seeds pooling a toolchain change (KB Decision 51): a preliminary estimate, not a confidence interval, and NOT a measurement of StructFormer variance, which remains unmeasured.

m6_gate.role: THE PRE-REGISTERED M6 EXIT GATE (KB Decision 55).
m6_gate.definition: Guard-band pairs whose median displacement is >= 1.0 px. The guard band is held out of BOTH splits, and the motion filter is what makes temporal error measure REPROJECTION rather than flicker.

pre_registered_threshold.rule: M6 passes if Model D's temporal error on this gate is at least 2 CNN across-seed sd below Model C's, AND its sharpness does not fall more than 1 sd below Model C's. Fixed before Model D is trained (KB Decision 55).

sharpness_guard.why: A blurrier renderer has trivially lower temporal error (KB Decision 53's RCS confound on a new metric). M6 must not win by softening.

motion_response_diagnostic.purpose: Whether TE measures warp quality AT ALL on this session, asked separately because the validation split cannot answer it: 43 of its 44 dt==1 pairs displace by under half a pixel.
motion_response_diagnostic.scope: Every pair in the session with >= 2 px median displacement, from any split. NOT A GATE and not part of any model comparison: it scores the native engine and the teacher targets ONLY, neither of which was fit to anything, so split membership does not apply to them. Trained models are excluded on purpose. Most qualifying frames fall in the 60-frame guard band, which belongs to no split — another reason the validation split cannot answer this question.

cnn_across_seed_spread.note: The number M6's margin is to be built from. Three Model A runs differing ONLY in seed, so this is run-to-run variance and nothing else. A Model D improvement smaller than this is not evidence (KB Decision 46).

frozen_note: FROZEN COPY, taken BEFORE Model D was scored. `m6_temporal_baseline.json` is the live artifact and now also contains Model D, because its generator scores every rung including D. That made Decision 57's 'threshold byte-identical before and after' unverifiable from the repo — it was true, but the evidence lived in a temp file. This file IS that evidence (KB Decision 58). Its m6_gate.sources deliberately contains NO m6_temporal_model_d.
